title: I made a solo card game about building a planetary system with Claude Code. Keeping the AI's memory was harder than anything else
author: wendeoo
selftext:
Proto Orbits is a solo card game where you build a planetary system over the life of a star. You place planetesimals, grow them into planets, add moons, keep the orbits stable and try to get life going before the star turns red giant, goes supernova or fries everything with pulsar radiation. It has 8 star types, a 40-level hand-designed campaign, daily and weekly challenges, and available in English and Portuguese.

Main mechanics were inspired by games heavy on rules, such as Civilization and Victoria series.

It's plain HTML/CSS/JS with no framework and no build step. It ships as a Windows .exe (Electron) and as a browser version. I did the design and the playtesting, and Claude Code wrote almost all of the code. Here's what made that work:

Long sessions get expensive and drift. I keep a .md file with the current rules, a file map, the architecture, open issues and *only the last 5 changes*. Every new chat starts with the same prompt: "Read project\_context.md, only check the files that matter, list pending items and wait." Early on that file kept the full history, and it got so bloated it was useless. Cutting it down to "current state + last 5 changes" was the single best change I made.

After every change, a bot plays 30 games per star and reports average scores, so balance swings show up right away. For the campaign, a solver searches for a 3-star solution for each level and saves it. The tests replay those solutions, so if a rule change breaks a level, I know immediately. The bot is weak at some things (it's bad at keeping life alive), so human playtesting still matters.

No scrolling anywhere (anything that doesn't fit gets split into pages), test in the browser, back up files before big changes, only build the .exe when I ask. Without written rules it would happily "improve" things I never asked it to touch.

The real struggle was: fitting the UI to the pixel without scrolling took many rounds of headless Chrome screenshots. Game feel and difficulty still came down to me playing it.

Wanna try it? It's free. I'd love to hear your thoughts. [https://deadpixstudios.itch.io/proto-orbits](https://deadpixstudios.itch.io/proto-orbits)

Question for you: how do you keep context across sessions on a bigger project? A file like mine, or something else?
